claim_ceiling: The market supports mainstream AI-assisted development, commercial human-supervised repository agents, emerging vendor-defined software-factory control planes, and active programmable harnesses. DomainSpec v2 currently supports a bounded typed-validation and same-host reproducible-realization kernel plus governed factory contracts; it does not yet establish an autonomous, operable, production-stable software factory.

market_signals: AI assistance is mainstream, but the evidence is broader than autonomous agents.
Agent use is growing while monitored single-agent operation and protected-action controls remain the defensible norm.
Independent trust signals remain materially weaker than adoption signals.
Vendor activity and platform telemetry do not establish market share or causal delivery improvement.

disagreements.resolution: Use the cohort for taxonomy; keep detailed cross-product architecture conclusions partial.
Commercial category existence is not local readiness or proof of a stable shared category.
Treat the operating model as future-work and individual owned kernels as build-from-owned only after blockers close.
Block the integrated branch while admitting decomposed bounded experiments.
Do not infer autonomous-factory adoption or market share from respondent use or platform telemetry.
